newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed prices ease with weaker soybeans.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed prices ease with weaker soybeans.

text.p: Nominal rapeseed prices in Northern Europe eased along with a weaker Chicago soybean complex, where exports and processing slowed while harvest forecasts pointed to good crops.
"Old crop trades are slim because crushers are reasonably well covered," one broker said.
"The new crop rapeseed market is unlikely to come to life as long as soybean values in the U.S. are still falling," he added.
Monday's USDA supply and demand report lessened concerns about tight supply.
June delivery old crop rapeseed free Hamburg was in a 497.50/490 marks a tonne seller/buyer range, down 15 marks on the week.
New crop free Hamburg was in a 462.50/454 marks range after trades at 465 marks were reported last week.
More rainfall in western Europe improved harvest prospects for oilseeds, which helped create a bearish tone.
Reports of winter damage were also less dramatic than previously expected.

The eastern German state of Mecklenburg said replantings in areas previously sown to winter rapeseed amounted to 0.8 percent, farm price office ZMP reported. Mecklenburg had to replant 19.9 percent of the area for the rapeseed harvest last year.
May buyers at points other than Hamburg were at 480-495 marks, down from 502-510 marks a week ago, with June at 495-500 (510-515) and August at 440-455 (455-465).
August rapeseed futures on the Matif exchange last traded at 455 marks, unchanged from last night and down 10 on the week.
Spot rape meal ex Hamburg mills was offered slightly lower at 31.00-31.25 marks per 100 kg fob, with June at 30.75, July at 30.50 and Aug-Oct at 26.00.
Rape oil sellers were at 92-93 marks per 100 kg for May-July, down 2.50-3.50, with Aug/Oct at 91.25-91.75, down 3.25-3.75.
